# Initialize
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(Seurat)
library(patchwork)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
# Load the PBMC dataset
colon.data <- sm
# Initialize the Seurat object with the raw (non-normalized data).
colon <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = colon.data, project = "colon", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)
colon1 <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = colon.data, project = "colon", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)

#notice that the parameters filter out all cells in which there are less than 200 genes expressed (min.features) and genes expressed in less that 3 cells (min.cells). The matrix will contain 13714 genes and 2700 cells. That is, an initial cell/gene removal. The parameters used are here usually not changed.
colon


```

```{r}
sm@Dimnames[[1]] <- sub("_[^_]*$", "", sm@Dimnames[[1]])
genenames <- rownames(sm)
rownames(sm) <- make.names(genenames, unique=TRUE)

colon <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = sm, project = "colon", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)
colon1 <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = sm, project = "colon", min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)


colon1
colon

rownames(colon)
```

## Quality control

```{r}
head(colnames(colon))

grep("^MT\\.",rownames(colon),value = TRUE)

grep("^MT",rownames(colon),value = TRUE)
```
```{r}
colon[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(colon, pattern = "^MT\\.")
head(colon)
```


```{r}
grep("^RP[LS]",rownames(colon),value = TRUE)
```

```{r}
colon[["percent.rbp"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(colon, pattern = "^RP[LS]")
head(colon)
```

```{r}
head(colon@meta.data, 5)
```

## Filtering out bad cells
QUA HO CAMBIATO TUTTO
```{r}
#colon <- subset(colon, subset = nFeature_RNA > 200 & nFeature_RNA < 2500 & percent.mt < 5)
colon <- subset(colon, subset = nFeature_RNA > 200 & nFeature_RNA < 6000 & percent.mt < 20)
```

### Cell Cycle genes
```{r}
cc.genes.updated.2019
```

```{r}
CellCycleScoring(colon, s.features = cc.genes.updated.2019$s.genes, g2m.features = cc.genes.updated.2019$g2m.genes, set.ident = TRUE) -> colon

colon[[]]
```

```{r}
#the default method -vst- computes (or better, estimates) the mean-variance relationship of each gene, and chooses the 2000 genes with hte highest variance. 
colon <- FindVariableFeatures(colon, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)

# Identify the 10 most highly variable genes
top10 <- head(VariableFeatures(colon), 10)

# plot variable features with and without labels
plot1 <- VariableFeaturePlot(colon)
plot1 <- LabelPoints(plot = plot1, points = top10, repel = TRUE)
plot1 
```

```{r}
all.genes <- rownames(colon)
colon <- ScaleData(colon, features = all.genes)
```

```{r}
colon@assays$RNA
```

```{r}
head(colon[["RNA"]]$scale.data["IL32",],20)
```

## Dimensional reduction
```{r}
colon <- RunPCA(colon, features = VariableFeatures(object = colon))
# Examine and visualize PCA results a few different ways
print(colon[["pca"]], dims = 1:5, nfeatures = 5)
```

```{r}
DimPlot(colon, reduction = "pca")
```
```{r}
VizDimLoadings(colon, dims = 1:2, reduction = "pca")
```


```{r}
ElbowPlot(colon, ndims=300)
```

```{r}
pc.touse <- (colon$pca@stdev)^2
pc.touse <- pc.touse/sum(pc.touse)
pc.touse <- cumsum(pc.touse)[1:1000]
pc.touse <- min(which(pc.touse>=0.8))

pc.touse
```

## clustering
```{r}
colon <- FindNeighbors(colon, dims = 1:25)

colon20 <- FindNeighbors(colon, dims = 1:20)
colon20_0.5 <- FindClusters(colon20, resolution = 0.5)
```

```{r}
colon@meta.data %>%
  group_by(seurat_clusters,Phase) %>%
  count() %>%
  group_by(seurat_clusters) %>%
  mutate(percent=100*n/sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=seurat_clusters,y=percent, fill=Phase)) +
  geom_col() +
  ggtitle("Percentage of cell cycle phases per cluster")
```
